node: Grid interconnection, transmission construction, utility power availability, nuclear/firm power, and data-center energy procurement
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the AI/data-center power-availability node. The reference lane is anchored by Quanta Services as the obvious grid-construction leader. The discovery lane emphasizes narrower or less universally owned public companies with direct exposure to medium-voltage switchgear, electrical construction, and nuclear-fuel availability: Powell Industries, MYR Group, and Centrus Energy. Key claim boundary: grid and power availability as a chokepoint is supported by recent industry reporting, but the degree to which each candidate converts AI/data-center demand into durable earnings remains an inference requiring backlog, customer, margin, and regulatory verification. Expanded the underfollowed lane around AI/data-center power constraints into four US-listed candidates tied to electrical distribution equipment, transmission/substation construction, data-center electrical/technology infrastructure, and conduit/cable-management components. The pass intentionally avoids hyperscalers, mega-cap utilities, and obvious grid leaders except as context. Key bottleneck logic: if powered land, interconnection timelines, transformer/switchgear availability, and substation construction become limiting factors, smaller electrical contractors and component suppliers may receive second-order demand before headline utility earnings fully reflect it. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the AI data-center power chokepoint while deliberately avoiding hyperscaler and mega-cap crowding.
